3509.explanation: The verdict is green, but only for the mirror-image repaired version of the best guess: all 8 raw guesses broke the chirality rule, and the repaired one has C2 matching the reactant. The mirror flip changes no interatomic distance, and the unrepaired guess has the same energy and frequencies, so a DFT frequency check would not have caught the wrong handedness. Next, use the repaired structure and not the raw model output. The models agree closely (0.024 A against a 0.109 A review cut-off), and the largest spread, 0.09 A at H8-H14, involves no forming or breaking bond.

5877.explanation: This guess is red: none of the 8 model guesses pass every rule, and all of them fail the product-stereo check. The recommended guess has the C2 stereocentre inverted relative to the product (its signed volume is +0.75 at the TS but -0.72 in the product), while C3 and C5 are correct. Mirroring cannot repair it, because only some of the stereocentres are wrong and a mirror image would flip the correct ones too, so re-generate the guess rather than patching it or sending it to DFT.

Next, run a DFT check on the recommended guess, and don't try a repair, since nothing in these facts says a particular fix would work.

The models also agree closely with each other, since the chosen guess differs from the others by only 0.022 Å on average, well under the 0.109 Å review cut-off, and the biggest spread is a small 0.04 Å on C6-H7, which isn't a forming or breaking bond. So you can reasonably trust this geometry and take it forward to your next step (for example DFT refinement or a frequency check), with no repair needed, though this verdict covers handedness and model agreement, not a guarantee that the geometry itself is exact.
